security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel or M-mode firmware writes to acliciprio[0] or aclicsourcecfg[0] via the Smaia/Ssaia indirect CSR access mechanism (xiselect/xireg), expecting the write to configure interrupt source 0 or target 0, but hardware silently drops the write because APLIC domains do not implement target[0] and aclicsourcecfg[0] is read-only zero
security_spec.summary: APLIC index-0 entities (acliciprio[0] target[0] bits, aclicsourcecfg[0]) are read-only zero; writes via indirect CSR (xiselect/xireg) are silently dropped, causing firmware/hypervisor to operate on stale assumed state for source 0

findings.finding: Kernel uses CSR_ISELECT/CSR_IREG only for IMSIC register range (isel 0x70-0xff, i.e. EIDELIVERY through EIE63 via IMSIC_FIRST..IMSIC_LAST). The ACLIC-specific ISELECT range 0x1000-0x10FF for acliciprio[0]/aclicsourcecfg[0] is never accessed. ISELECT writes are bounded by the caller's isel computation (id / BITS_PER_LONG * 32 + EIP0/EIE0 base).

spec_citations.excerpt: | 0x1000 | 4B | acliciprio0 | ... Indirect access to acliciprio[k] mirror target[k*4].iprio up to target[k*4+3].iprio.
APLIC domains do not implement target[0]. When accessing acliciprio[0], the bits corresponding to target[0] are read-only zero.
| 0x1000 | 4B | aclicsourcecfg0 | ... Access to aclicsourcecfg[0][15:0] is read-only zero.

findings.finding: KVM's SIREG read-modify-write handler dispatches on VSISELECT value: handles IPRIO range (isel 0x30-0x3f) and IMSIC range (0x70-0xff). For all other ISELECT values — including the ACLIC range 0x1000-0x10FF — it returns KVM_INSN_EXIT_TO_USER_SPACE, correctly deferring unknown indirect registers to userspace rather than silently dropping writes.

APLIC hardware init correctly starts from source 1 (i=1; i<=nr_irqs), using register offset (i-1)*sizeof(u32). The first writel targets SOURCECFG_BASE+0 = 0x0004 = sourcecfg[1], and TARGET_BASE+0 = 0x3004 = target[1]. Source 0 (which would be at offset 0x0000 relative to the base-0 register map) is never touched.

spec_citations.excerpt: APLIC domains do not implement target[0].

findings.finding: Save/restore uses 0-based array index with register offset i*sizeof(u32), so srcs[0] maps to SOURCECFG_BASE+0 = 0x0004 = sourcecfg[1] and TARGET_BASE+0 = 0x3004 = target[1]. The comment at line 38-42 explicitly acknowledges the AIA spec rule that target[i] is RO-zero when source i is inactive. No attempt to write to hardware source 0 (the non-existent register at offset 0x0000 or 0x3000).

KVM virtualized APLIC enforces '!irq || aplic->nr_irqs <= irq' guard, rejecting source index 0 on all per-IRQ accessors (sourcecfg, target, pending, enabled, input). The MMIO dispatch maps offset i = ((off-APLIC_SOURCECFG_BASE)>>2)+1, converting register offset 0 to source index 1. Consistent with APLIC spec: source 0 is reserved/nonexistent.

spec_citations.excerpt: APLIC domains do not implement target[0].

findings.finding: KVM MMIO read/write dispatch for APLIC uses (nr_irqs - 1)*4 as the upper bound for sourcecfg/target MMIO ranges, meaning offset 0 maps to source index 1 and the last offset maps to source nr_irqs-1. Array bounds correctly enforced via the per-IRQ functions' !irq check.

ISELECT_IPRIO0..IPRIO15 defined as 0x30-0x3f (standard AIA indirect CSR range for interrupt priority), with ISELECT_MASK = GENMASK(8,0) limiting valid selectors to 9 bits (0x00-0x1ff). This range cannot alias to the ACLIC-specific ISELECT range 0x1000-0x10FF where acliciprio[0] and aclicsourcecfg[0] reside — the ACLIC range requires 13-bit ISELECT values.
